prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create one new episode scene in the same manuscript illustration series.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Episode 14: Avtandil's Testament, Prayer & Secret Flight from Arabia.
Setting: Arabia, Avtandil’s house and the quiet city gate just before dawn.
Single coherent scene: Avtandil entrusts a small completely unmarked folded parchment packet tied with plain cord to loyal Shermadin. His saddled horse waits in shadow while the first pale light catches the palace arches, conveying the secret departure and the testament left behind.
Characters in scene: Avtandil, a young clean-shaven man with wavy chestnut hair, thoughtful brown eyes, the face of reference 2, a vermilion travel cloak over practical Georgian-Eastern clothes; Shermadin, a sturdy slightly older short-bearded man in the navy cap and blue-gold quilted coat of reference 3.
Story constraints: Rostevan and Sograt do not witness the secret flight. The testament is represented by a closed blank folded packet, never a written page or rolled scroll.
Reference roles: image1 is STYLE ONLY: match the luminous mineral pigments, gold floral detail, faceted space, fine contours and aged ivory edge vignette. Do not include its poet. Images2 and3 are IDENTITY references for Avtandil and Shermadin; remove all circular portrait rims and integrate them as full courtly figures in the narrative scene.
Composition: a full horizontal 16:10 painting, native approximately1600x1000. Avtandil and Shermadin exchange the plain small folded paper packet near center-left under a palace arch; the saddled horse and open gate recede at right in pale dawn. Their hands and faces stay fully visible and anatomically natural. The packet is CLOSED AND COMPLETELY BLANK, not a scroll or document with writing. No extra named characters.
STRICTLY NO TEXT, LETTERS, CAPTIONS, NUMBERS, CALLIGRAPHY, INSCRIPTIONS, BANNERS, FLAGS, SCROLLS, WATERMARKS. No pseudo-script in architectural ornament.

visual_qa.notes: Avtandil gives blank closed packet to Shermadin; saddled horse and dawn gateway; only the two co-present named figures.
